headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
I don’t have live access to a movie‑listing database right now, so I can’t pull the exact titles that are playing at a given moment. However, I can give you a quick guide on how to find a film that meets your criteria and point out a few nearby theaters where you’re likely to see a good selection of short‑running movies.

---

## 1. Pick a nearby theater

Times Square is surrounded by several major multiplexes that show a wide range of films:

| Theater | Address | Approx. walking distance |
|---------|---------|--------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** | 234 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.3 mi (≈5–7 min walk) |
| **Regal Cinemas Times Square** | 225 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.3 mi |
| **Cinemark 18 Times Square** | 200 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.3 mi |
| **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema** (a bit farther, but still within a 10‑minute walk) | 151 W 45th St, New York, NY 10036 | ~0.6 mi |

All of these venues have online booking pages where you can filter by showtime and sometimes by runtime.

---

## 2. How to find a film ≤ 2 hours

1. **Go to the theater’s website**  
   * AMC Empire 25: `https://www.amctheatres.com/movie-theaters/amc-empire-25`  
   * Regal Times Square: `https://www.regmovies.com/theater/ny/regal-cinemas-times-square`  
   * Cinemark 18: `https://www.cinemark.com/cinemark-18-times-square`

2. **Select “Now Showing” or “Showtimes.”**  
   Most sites let you choose a date and then display all current screenings.

3. **Look for the “Runtime” column** (or click on a movie title to see details).  
   If the site doesn’t list runtimes directly, you can:
   * Click the title → “Details” → “Runtime” field.  
   * Or use a quick Google search: `"Movie Title" runtime`.

4. **Filter by showtime**  
   Pick a time that works for you (e.g., 7 pm, 9 pm).  
   If you’re looking for a “short” film, many theaters show indie or documentary shorts that are 90 min or less.

5. **Book tickets**  
   Once you’ve found a suitable film, reserve seats online or via the theater’s mobile app.

---

## 3. Quick “starter” list (as of early 2024)

Below are a few titles that were playing in NYC around this time and are under 2 hours. (Check the theater sites for current availability.)

| Title | Runtime | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| **“The Last Full Measure”** | 1h 52m | Drama about a WWII hero; often shown in AMC Empire 25. |
| **“The Last of Us” (TV series)** | 1h 30m per episode | If you’re into gaming‑based storytelling; AMC has a special screening. |
| **“The Great” (TV series)** | 1h 20m per episode | Comedy‑drama; AMC’s “Great” marathon. |
| **“The Last of Us: Part II” (short film)** | 1h 15m | Indie short; check Cinemark 18. |
| **“The Last of Us: The Final Chapter” (documentary)** | 1h 45m | Documentary about the game’s impact; shown at Regal. |

> **Tip:** Many theaters also host “short‑film festivals” or “indie nights” where the entire program is under 2 hours. Look for those events on the theater’s calendar.

---

## 4. Alternative: Use a movie‑search engine

If you prefer a single place to search across multiple theaters:

* **Fandango** (`https://www.fandango.com`) – enter “Times Square” as the location, then filter by “Runtime” (under 120 min).  
* **Google Movies** – type “movies near Times Square” into Google, then use the “Runtime” filter on the results page.  
* **MovieTickets.com** – similar filtering options.

---

### Bottom line

- **Pick a theater** (AMC Empire 25, Regal Times Square, Cinemark 18).  
- **Search their “Now Showing” page** and look for runtimes ≤ 120 minutes.  
- **Book online** once you find a film that fits your schedule.

Enjoy your movie night in NYC! If you’d like me to help you locate a specific film or check a particular theater’s schedule, just let me know the theater name and the date you’re interested in.
